daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Price Momentum Analysis with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a SQL query that calculates a 5-day moving average and identifies stocks that have gained more than 10% over the last 20 trading days. Use window functions (AVG() OVER, ROW_NUMBER() OVER) and a CTE to rank stocks by momentum. Your output should show: stock_code, current_price, 5day_moving_avg, 20day_return_pct, and momentum_rank. Order by momentum_rank ascending.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Incident Aggregation
daily_quests.description: Download the NSW Road Crash dataset and clean it thoroughly: handle missing values in crash location and severity columns (decide: drop vs. impute), standardise crash_type values (remove whitespace, convert to uppercase), remove duplicate crash_id records, and convert date columns to datetime format. Then aggregate crashes by suburb and crash_type to produce a summary table showing crash_count, avg_severity_score, and date_range per suburb. Export to cleaned_crashes_summary.csv.

daily_quests.title: Melbourne Pedestrian Traffic Analysis: Python ETL + SQL Analytics
daily_quests.description: Part 1 (Python): Extract Melbourne pedestrian counting data, parse the timestamp column, resample to hourly foot traffic counts, and load into a SQLite database table called pedestrian_traffic (columns: sensor_id, location_name, traffic_datetime, hourly_count). Part 2 (SQL): Query the database to find peak traffic hours (top 3 hours by total count), identify which sensor locations have the most consistent traffic using variance, and create a summary showing location_name, peak_hour, avg_hourly_count, and consistency_score (inverse of variance). Export results to peak_traffic_analysis.csv. This simulates a real data pipeline: ingest → transform → load → analyse.
